subject: non-normality in model without latent variables

messages.author: fe83e3e0b62fd43e
messages.subject: non-normality in model without latent variables
parts:
Hello,

I am pretty new to lavaan, so forgive me if my question will sound a bit stupid.
I noticed that the use of MLR estimator instead of default ML results in different fit indices, but it does not affect the estimation of regression and correlation coefficients. Having to perform a model without latent variables (in which I am not interested in fit indices) and having to deal with the non-normality of the distribution of my data, how can I do? 

Thank you in advice

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: non-normality in model without latent variables
parts:
You can use MLR as you already did.  MLR does not adjust the point estimates (those are not biased by nonnormality), but it adjusts the standard errors (SE) so that the p-values associated with your estimates have closer to nominal Type I error rates.

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c

On 05/25/2014 06:45 PM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
> You can use MLR as you already did. MLR does not adjust the point
> estimates (those are not biased by nonnormality), but it adjusts the
> standard errors (SE) so that the p-values associated with your estimates
> have closer to nominal Type I error rates.

and it scales the chi-square test statistic (in the `Robust' column),
which affects many fit indices (CFI, RMSEA, but not SRMR)

Yves.
